edition.copy_text: Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI

source_text: Μετὰ ταῦτα δὲ τοιαύτην ἐκτίθεται περὶ Ἰουδαίων λέξιν· πρῶτον οὖν τῶν Ἰουδαίων θαυμάζειν ἄξιον, εἰ τὸν μὲν οὐρανὸν καὶ τοὺς ἐν τῷδε ἀγγέλους σέβουσι, τὰ σεμνότατα δὲ αὐτοῦ μέρη καὶ δυνατώτατα, ἥλιον καὶ σελήνην καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους ἀστέρας ἀπλανεῖς τε καὶ πλανήτας, ταῦτα παραπέμπουσιν· ὡς ἐνδεχόμε νον τὸ μὲν ὅλον εἶναι θεὸν, τὰ δὲ μέρη αὐτοῦ μὴ θεῖα. ἢ τοὺς μὲν ἐν σκότῳ που ἐκ γοητείας οὐκ ὀρθῆς τυφλώττουσιν ἢ δι᾿ ἀμυδρῶν φασμάτων ὀνειρώττουσιν ἐγχρίμπτειν λεγομένους εὖ μάλα θρησκεύειν, τοὺς δ᾿ ἐναργῶς οὕτως καὶ λαμπρῶς ἅπασι προφητεύοντας, δι᾿ ὧν ὑετούς τε καὶ θάλπη καὶ νέφη καὶ βροντὰς, ἃς προσκυνοῦσι, καὶ ἀστραπὰς καὶ καρποὺς καὶ γονὰς ἁπάσας ταμιεύεσθαι, δι᾿ ὧν αὐτοῖς ἀνακαλύπτεσθαι τὸν θεὸν, τοὺς φανερωτάτους τῶν ἄνω κήρυκας, τοὺς ὡς ἀληθῶς οὐρανίους ἀγγέλους, τούτους ἡγεῖσθαι τὸ μηδέν, ἐν τούτοις δὲ δοκεῖ μοι συγκεχύσθαι ὁ Κέλσος καὶ ἀπὸ παρακουσμάτων ἃ μὴ ᾔδει γεγραφέναι· σαφὲς γὰρ τοῖς τὰ Ἰουδαίων ἐξετάζουσι καὶ τὰ Χριστιανῶν ἐκείνοις συνάπτουσιν ὅτι τῷ μὲν νόμῳ ἀκολουθοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι, λέγοντι ἐκ προσώπου θεοῦ· „οὐκ ἔσονταί σοι (θεοὶ) ἕτεροι πλὴν ἐμοῦ, οὐ ποιήσεις σεαυτῷ εἴδωλον οὐδὲ παντὸς ὁμοίωμα, ὅσα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἄνω καὶ ὅσα ἐν τῇ γῇ κάτω καὶ ὅσα ἐν τοῖς ὕδασιν ὑποκάτω τῆς γῆς· οὐ προσκυνήσεις αὐτοῖς οὐδὲ μὴ λατρεύσῃς αὐτοῖς,“ οὐδὲν ἄλλο σέβουσιν ἢ τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεὸν, ὃς ἐποίησε τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ πάντα, δῆλον δ᾿ ὅτι οἱ κατὰ τὸν νόμον βιοῦντες σέβοντες τὸν ποιήσαντα τὸν οὐρανὸν οὐ συσσέβουσι τῷ θεῷ τὸν οὐρανόν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἀγγέλους οὐδεὶς τῶν δουλευόντων τῷ Μωϋσέως νόμῳ προσκυνεῖ· ὁμοίως δὲ τῷ μὴ προσκυνεῖν ἥλιον καὶ σελήνην καὶ τοὺς ἀστέρας, „τὸν κόσμον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ“, ἀπέχονται τοῦ προσκυνεῖν οὐρανὸν καὶ τοὺς ἐν αὐτῷ ἀγγέλους, πειθόμενοι τῷ λέγοντι νόμῳ· „καὶ μὴ ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν ἥλιον καὶ τὴν σελήνην καὶ τοὺς ἀστέρας, πάντα τὸν κόσμον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, πλανηθεὶς προσκυνήσῃς αὐτοῖς καὶ λατρεύσῃς αὐτοῖς, ἃ ἀπένειμε κύριος ὁ θεός σου αὐτὰ πᾶσι τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.“
pass_a_gloss: After these things he sets out (ἐκτίθημι) such a saying (λέξις) about Jews: 'First then it is worth wondering at (θαυμάζειν ἄξιον) of the Jews, if they revere (σέβω) the heaven (οὐρανός) and the angels in it, but the most venerable (σεμνότατος) and most powerful (δυνατώτατος) parts (μέρη) of it, sun and moon and the other stars, both fixed (ἀπλανεῖς) and planets (πλανῆται), these they pass by (παραπέμπω); as though it were possible (ἐνδέχομαι) for the whole (τὸ ὅλον) to be god but its parts not divine (θεῖα). Or [that they] worship very well (εὖ μάλα θρησκεύω) those said to approach (ἐγχρίμπτω) somewhere in darkness (σκότος) those blinded (τυφλώττω) from an incorrect (οὐκ ὀρθή) sorcery (γοητεία) or dreaming (ὀνειρώττω) through dim (ἀμυδρός) phantoms (φάσματα), but those prophesying (προφητεύω) so clearly (ἐναργῶς) and brightly (λαμπρῶς) to all, through whom rains (ὑετοί) and heats (θάλπη) and clouds and thunders (βρονταί), which they worship (προσκυνέω), and lightnings and fruits and all generations/offspring (γοναί) are dispensed (ταμιεύω), through whom God is revealed (ἀνακαλύπτω) to them, the most manifest (φανερώτατοι) heralds (κήρυκες) of the things above, the truly heavenly (οὐράνιοι) angels, these to consider (ἡγέομαι) nothing (τὸ μηδέν).' In these things Celsus seems to me to have been confused (συγχέω) and to have written from things misheard (παρακούσματα) what he did not know; for it is clear to those examining (ἐξετάζω) the things of the Jews and joining (συνάπτω) those of the Christians to them that, following the law (νόμος) which says from the person (πρόσωπον) of God: 'There shall not be to you other (θεοί, suppl.) besides me; you shall not make for yourself an idol (εἴδωλον) nor a likeness (ὁμοίωμα) of anything, as many as are in the heaven above and as many as are in the earth below and as many as are in the waters beneath the earth; you shall not worship them nor serve (λατρεύω) them,' the Jews revere nothing else than the God over all, who made the heaven and all the rest; and it is clear that those living by the law, revering the one who made the heaven, do not co-revere (συσσέβω) the heaven with God, but also none of those serving (δουλεύω) the law of Moses worships the angels in heaven; and in like manner to not worshipping sun and moon and the stars, 'the array/adornment (κόσμος) of heaven,' they abstain from worshipping heaven and the angels in it, obeying the law which says: 'And lest, having looked up (ἀναβλέπω) to heaven and having seen the sun and the moon and the stars, all the array of heaven, having been led astray (πλανάω) you worship them and serve them, which the Lord your God distributed (ἀπονέμω) to all the nations (ἔθνη).'

choices.english: And do not, when you look up to heaven and see …, be led astray
rejected: And do not look up to heaven and, seeing …, be led astray
choices.why: μή governs προσκυνήσῃς, not the participle ἀναβλέψας; the old wording forbade looking up
speaker split checked: Celsus from ‘First, then’ to ‘as nothing’, Origen from ‘In these remarks’

pass_b_english: After this he sets out a passage about the Jews, as follows: “First, then, one may well wonder at the Jews, that they revere heaven and the angels in it, yet pass over the most venerable and most powerful parts of it, the sun and the moon and the other stars, both fixed and wandering; as if it were possible for the whole to be a god while its parts are not divine. Or that they worship most devoutly beings who are said to draw near, somewhere in the dark, to people blinded by a crooked sorcery or dreaming through dim phantoms, while those who prophesy so plainly and so brilliantly to all, through whom rains and heat and clouds and thunders (which they worship) and lightnings and fruits and every kind of offspring are dispensed, through whom God is revealed to them, the most manifest heralds of the world above, the truly heavenly angels, these they count as nothing.”

In these remarks Celsus seems to me to be confused, and to have written, from things he heard amiss, about matters he did not know. For it is clear to those who examine the ways of the Jews and set those of the Christians beside them that the Jews follow the law, which says in the person of God: “You shall have no other gods besides me. You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor a likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is on the earth beneath, or that is in the waters under the earth. You shall not worship them, nor serve them” (Exodus 20:3–5). Following this law, they revere nothing but the God over all, who made heaven and everything else.

And it is plain that those who live by the law, revering the One who made heaven, do not revere heaven together with God; nor does anyone who serves the law of Moses worship the angels in heaven either. Just as they do not worship the sun and the moon and the stars, “the array of heaven,” so they abstain from worshipping heaven and the angels in it, obeying the law which says: “And do not, when you look up to heaven and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the array of heaven, be led astray and worship them and serve them, things which the Lord your God has allotted to all the nations” (Deuteronomy 4:19).
notes: Celsus’s passage runs from πρῶτον οὖν to τὸ μηδέν; Origen’s reply begins at ἐν τούτοις δὲ δοκεῖ μοι. Celsus’s sentence changes construction midway (θαυμάζειν ἄξιον εἰ … then accusative-and-infinitive θρησκεύειν … ἡγεῖσθαι); rendered ‘Or that they …’ to keep his dependence on ‘one may well wonder’. ‘Which they worship’ refers grammatically to the thunders (ἃς … βροντάς), as Celsus has it. Exodus 20:3–5 (first half of v. 5) is quoted in LXX wording; the parallel Deuteronomy 5:7–9 is near identical. θεοὶ in Exodus 20:3 is a bracketed supplement in Koetschau’s text, followed (it is in the LXX). Deuteronomy 4:19 LXX quoted, ending before τοῖς ὑποκάτω τοῦ οὐρανοῦ. ‘Array of heaven’ renders LXX ὁ κόσμος τοῦ οὐρανοῦ (Hebrew ‘host of heaven’); ‘array’ keeps both order and adornment. ‘In the person of God’ = ἐκ προσώπου θεοῦ. ‘Fixed and wandering’ = ἀπλανεῖς τε καὶ πλανήτας. ‘Every kind of offspring’ renders γονὰς ἁπάσας (births, generation of living things).

changes: Deuteronomy 4:19: ‘And do not look up to heaven and, seeing …, be led astray’ -> ‘And do not, when you look up to heaven and see …, be led astray’ (μή governs προσκυνήσῃς, not the participle ἀναβλέψας; the old wording forbade looking up)
